articles.summary: Medicaid notices come in many forms - coverage denials, fair-hearing rights, copay changes, plan assignments, service authorizations, and the annual renewal - but they share a problem: each one asks someone, often someone managing a chronic condition, working two jobs, or caring for a child, to understand what's happening and frequently to act on it.
articles.title: What Does a Medicaid Notice Actually Look Like?

articles.summary: In June 2026, CMS released the interim final rule implementing the new Medicaid community engagement requirement created by Section 71119 of the Working Families Tax Cut (WFTC) legislation. This is the most significant change to Medicaid eligibility since expansion, and it introduces a work-or-activity requirement as a condition of coverage for many adult Medicaid members.
articles.title: What the CMS Interim Final Rule Means for Health Plans and Health Systems

articles.summary: Three panels at this year's AHIP Annual Conference kept arriving at the same uncomfortable conclusion. A tough financial environment alongside a fast-approaching January 1, 2027 deadline. The plans best positioned to navigate new requirements under the “One Big Beautiful Bill” and H.R. 1 aren't scrambling to build something new… they’re continuously building on infrastructure from the past.
articles.title: Back to Basics: How Health Plans Are Rebuilding for H.R. 1 Under Pressure
